fixed.problem: [blocker] The merge step replayed a branch that carried another task's work. When main moved it rebased the PR branch and force-pushed it, so a dependent task's branch (built with its dependency's unmerged branch merged in) got the dependency's commits copied. Those commits never reached main as themselves, GitHub never marked the dependency's PR merged, and merging it later conflicted.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/merge-record.test.ts: '(a) a dependent branch whose base moved is merged as it is, with a merge commit: nothing replayed or forced, the dependency's commit reaches main once and both PRs are merged' and '(a) a rule that the branch be up to date brings main in by merging (a normal push), the record moves to the new head, and the retry merges it once its checks pass'. Before: the dependency PR stayed open, and the up-to-date head was a single-parent rebased commit.
fixed.how: mergeChecked (packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts) never rebases and never force-pushes. A base that moved is merged as it is with a merge commit, and GitHub combines the two. Only when an update is needed (a strict required-checks rule, or the gate's `update` flag) is main merged into the branch in the worktree: a merge commit and a normal push, `conflict` with the files when it does not merge cleanly, and back to the reviewed head when bringing main in changed the own change. The record then moves to the new head, and the reviewed head's checks must pass there. The testenv fake host now marks a PR merged when its head reaches the base inside another merge, as GitHub does.

fixed.problem: [blocker] The reviewed version was not saved. mergeReviewed took the worktree's HEAD as the reviewed commit whenever it ran, and its own rebase moved that HEAD. A retry, or a crash in the middle, could merge a commit nobody reviewed.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/merge-record.test.ts '(b) the reviewed version holds: a commit pushed after the accept is never merged by the retry' and '(b) a crash after main was merged in: the head keeps the task's own change, so the record moves to it and the retry merges it'. Before there was no record and no retry.
fixed.how: New table merge_record (migration 0006, MergeRecordRepo pin/move/claim/forAgent/forTask). mergeReviewed pins reviewed_head_sha (the worktree HEAD at the accept), reviewed_base_sha and own_change_id. It does this first, in every mode and at every level. own_change_id comes from capabilities ownChangeId: the patch id of the task's own diff without context lines, measured from DEPS_BASE_REF, from the marker merged with main once main was merged in, or from the fork point. Every merge is pinned to the record's sha. A moved PR head moves the record only when its own change id is unchanged. Anything else is head_moved, left to the person with one sentence and one card. With no worktree at the accept the reviewed version is unknown: the record goes to left_to_you as unverified and is never merged unattended.

fixed.problem: [blocker] A waiting merge was lost. If the checks were still running when the session's wait ended, the step filed a card and wrote only the task's reason text. fixed.how: A merge that waits keeps its record in waiting_checks, with the sentence "#4 merges when its checks pass." and no card. GitHostWatcher.poll() calls a new `retryMerges` dep (ReviewedPrMerge.retryWaiting). That pass tries each waiting or queued record of the install's own agent once, with no inline wait, and does nothing while Stop all holds the agent. resumeAtStart, called next to recoverInterruptedSessions in compose, settles records left `merging`: merged on the host becomes merged, closed becomes left_to_you, open goes back to waiting. Every record left to the person has a sentence, including not_allowed and unverified. Cards are filed once per record, only where the person must act. After about a day of tries a stuck record goes to the person. A stop or an unexpected error never leaves a record stuck in `merging`.

fixed.problem: [major] A retry outside a session had no authority of its own: the token and the wait were derived from the session's. A record kept per install also has to say whose it is, because the state can be the shared Postgres store.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/merge-record.test.ts '(c) ... the retry merges it with no session on its own narrow token, one audit row each; another agent's record is not touched' and '(d) the gate reads the level at every call: a record made at level 3, the level then lowered to 2, is not merged by the retry'
fixed.how: mergeRecorded(record, authority) is the only merge entry. It asks mayMerge(project, record, authority) first, re-reading the project each time: today unattended only at level 3 or above, and a person's click always, as an approval added for exactly that merge_pr call. A refusal writes one audit row on the hooks' audit port. Outside a session the call runs on tokens.issue: merge_pr only, that worktree, the git host's domain only, no secrets, budget 0, ten minutes, the project's current level, session id merge-<record id>. The token is revoked after the call and goes through beforeToolCall unchanged. The record carries agent_id, and only the install's agents (ReviewedPrMergeDeps.agentIds) are retried or resumed. claim() is optimistic on the row's version, so two daemons never merge one PR twice.

fixed.problem: [major] Nothing read the branch's rules. GitHub does not let a PR's author approve it, an admin is exempt from classic protection by default, and merging a dependent PR marks its dependency merged. An automatic merge or an admin token could go around the person's own rules.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/merge-record.test.ts '(e) a rule that needs an approving review: nothing merges, even on an admin token that GitHub would let around classic protection; one sentence and one card' (before: the admin token merged around classic protection); packages/capabilities/test/merge-commits.test.ts 'reads a ruleset's rules ...' and 'reads classic protection as an admin ...'
fixed.how: A new GitHost.getBranchRules(repo, branch) reads the rulesets (GET /rules/branches/{branch}; a 404 counts as none) and, when the token may read it, the classic protection, with the branch's `protected` flag and visible checks for anyone. It returns required approvals, code owners, required checks, up-to-date, allowed methods, blockers in words, and `unreadable` when the token is an admin's but the protection cannot be read. rulesBlock turns these into blocked_by_rules or merge_commits_off with one sentence, unattended and on a click alike, never with an admin bypass. Required checks are waited for as checks. The testenv fake host serves the rules route and classic protection (an admin's read only) and applies both on merge, with admin bypass of classic protection unless enforce_admins.

fixed.how:
Root cause: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/windows.rs new_window_action returned Refuse for any URL that navigation_allowed covers, the app's own pages included. Nothing sent such a page back to the existing window.

Fix:
- new_window_action now answers a new variant, LeaveAction::ShowHere(route), for a page on the app's origins. It uses deeplink::on_app_origin, which I factored out of navigation_allowed without changing what it does.
- windows::app_route() builds the route from the page's path, query and fragment. A path starting with // or /\ gets no route, because it would read as another host.
- leave() handles ShowHere through show_here(). That evaluates deeplink::navigate_script(route) on the main window from a spawned task, off the webview's own new-window handler. The script uses history.pushState plus popstate, which React Router follows, the same way as deep links and the tray's Updates entry.
- So the move is client-side, like a plain click: the page keeps its daemon token and nothing reloads.
- The shell logs "shown in this window (new window): <url>" (windows::shown_in_window_line, query left out).
- about:blank and the splash are still refused. Web pages still go to the system browser. No second window is ever created.
